item.title: Ant International launches Whale Orchestration Protocol linking DBS, Franklin Templeton tokens
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Singapore-based fintech company Ant International has launched the Whale Orchestration Protocol, an upgrade to its blockchain-based wholesale settlement platform WhaleRTP.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore-based fintech company Ant International has launched the Whale Orchestration Protocol, an upgrade to its blockchain-based wholesale settlement platform WhaleRTP.

In a statement on Thursday, Ant International said the protocol lets tokenized deposits and tokenized money market funds settle against each other in a single atomic transaction, known as delivery versus payment.

The protocol was developed under the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS)’s BLOOM initiative, which aims to build next-generation settlement infrastructure for domestic and cross-border payments. BLOOM stands for borderless, liquid, open, online, and multi-currency.

Ant International said it has completed pilot transactions with DBS and Franklin Templeton, which have integrated their tokenized treasury products into WhaleRTP. The pilot is the first successful cross-asset interoperability between tokenized deposits and money market funds in Singapore.

Kelvin Li, general manager of platform technology and senior vice president at Ant International, said 24/7 real-time liquidity management is essential to the company’s business. The firm wants to scale the solution with more partners.

Rachel Chew, COO and co-head of digital assets at DBS’s global transaction services, said tokenized money must go beyond payments and settlement. “By linking DBS Treasury Tokens with tokenized money market funds, we are demonstrating how tokenized deposits can power real-time liquidity and investment flows,” she said.

Sandy Kaul, head of innovation at Franklin Templeton, said the collaboration connects tokenized investment products to payment and settlement infrastructure. “By enabling interoperability between tokenized deposits and money market funds, we are helping move the industry closer to a future where capital can be deployed more efficiently, securely and in real time,” she said.

The three companies lead the BLOOM workstream on cross-asset interoperability. The BLOOM Field Guide, which provides a common framework for digital money, was presented at the Singapore FinTech Festival.

Ant International completes live cross-bank tokenised deposit transfers with 3 Hong Kong banks under EnsembleTX

item.title: Malaysia’s SkyeChip, France’s SiPearl to jointly develop next-generation compute platform
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: SkyeChip Berhad, a Malaysia-headquartered chip design company, and SiPearl, a France-based fabless designer of processors for supercomputing and AI, will cooperate to develop a next-generation compute platform based on Arm Neoverse Compute Subsystems.
item.content:encoded:
SkyeChip Berhad, a Malaysia-headquartered chip design company, and SiPearl, a France-based fabless designer of processors for supercomputing and AI, will cooperate to develop a next-generation compute platform based on Arm Neoverse Compute Subsystems.

In a statement on Tuesday, SkyeChip said both sides have signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding for the move. The MoU was signed on the sidelines of French President Emmanuel Macron’s visit to Malaysia, in the presence of Macron and Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

The companies plan to work through a joint venture to be incorporated in Malaysia, targeted for December 2026. SkyeChip would hold 51 percent and SiPearl 49 percent. The venture would combine SiPearl’s system architecture and server CPU expertise with SkyeChip’s silicon IP, including high-bandwidth memory interface, network-on-chip, and die-to-die interface IP.

Through the joint venture, they will apply for the Arm Neoverse CSS licence. If it is granted, they plan to define the platform specification, then carry out silicon development, tape-out, and post-silicon work toward production.

The cooperation depends on definitive agreements, which the companies intend to negotiate within 90 days of the MoU, along with board approvals at both companies and regulatory and export control clearances. These include the Arm Neoverse CSS licence.

Dato’ Fong Swee Kiang, CEO and founder of SkyeChip, said the partnership would help accelerate development, optimize costs and widen the company’s market reach in Asia, North America, and Europe.

Philippe Notton, CEO and founder of SiPearl, said the company’s first-generation CPU, Rhea1, has strengthened its position as a leader in Arm technology. SiPearl can offer resilient, high-performance, and secure processors to regions seeking alternatives.

SiPearl’s first-generation CPU, Rhea1, is due for release at the end of 2026. It can power the JUPITER supercomputer in Germany and the Alice Recoque in France. SiPearl employs 200 people in France, Spain, Italy and Taiwan.

Gobi-backed Malaysian IC firm SkyeChip jumps in IPO debut

item.title: AI company LinqAlpha opens Tokyo office, seeks cooperation with financial institutions
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: LinqAlpha, an AI company that builds research tools for public-market investors, has opened an office in Tokyo, in order to strengthen its presence in Asia and bring its AI-powered investment research closer to Japanese financial institutions.
item.content:encoded:
LinqAlpha, an AI company that builds research tools for public-market investors, has opened an office in Tokyo, in order to strengthen its presence in Asia and bring its AI-powered investment research closer to Japanese financial institutions.

In a statement on Wednesday, LinqAlpha said the Tokyo office joins LinqAlpha’s existing offices in New York, Singapore, Hong Kong, London, and Seoul. The platform already covers Japanese financial information extensively, reflecting the importance of Japanese companies and suppliers to global portfolios.

LinqAlpha also appointed Ryoichi Nomoto as its country general manager for Japan. Nomoto previously held roles at S&P Global and Bloomberg and has experience in financial data and its use at large financial institutions. He will lead business development, market expansion, and building relationships with local institutions.

LinqAlpha’s platform uses AI agents to analyze company filings, earnings transcripts, broker research, news, financial data and alternative data. The tools can also produce meeting notes, automated briefings and alerts. Japanese earnings disclosures and calls can be analyzed in their original language, with research outputs in English.

The company cited a Bank of Japan survey of 150 financial institutions in 2026, which found more than 90 percent were using or trialling generative AI. Those institutions still identify challenges around governance, third-party risk, safety and security. LinqAlpha aims to serve asset managers, pension funds, insurers, securities firms, trust banks, and wealth managers.

Jacob Chanyeol Choi, co-founder and co-CEO of LinqAlpha, said Japan is an important market for global investors and that a Tokyo presence is a natural next step.

Nomoto said Japanese financial institutions are increasingly exploring how AI can support investment research. The opportunity is to apply the technology in ways that are reliable and fit each institution’s approach.

LinqAlpha  launched an AI research lab in August 2026. The lab has published more than a dozen peer-reviewed papers at research venues including NeurIPS, ICLR, EMNLP, and ACM ICAIF, and studies the conditions under which AI-generated analysis can be trusted for investment decisions. The lab is led by Yongjae Lee, an associate professor at UNIST in Korea.

The expansion follows LinqAlpha’s $22 million Series A round in July 2026. The company serves more than 70 financial institutions across the United States, Europe and Asia. Its buy-side clients manage more than $5 trillion in assets.

AI can help portfolio managers work at “superhuman” level, says LinqAlpha founder [Q&A]

item.title: Canadia Impact Fund backs 2 technology startups Choose & Connect, DOCONCHAIN at FrancoTech
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Canadia Impact Fund will invest in two technology start-ups, the French education platform Choose & Connect and the document-verification company DOCONCHAIN.
item.content:encoded:
Canadia Impact Fund will invest in two technology start-ups, the French education platform Choose & Connect and the document-verification company DOCONCHAIN.

In two statement last Sunday, Canadia Impact Fund said it signed investment agreements with the two startups at FrancoTech, the innovation exhibition held at Koh Pich during the 20th Francophonie Summit. The fund did not disclose any financial details.

Canadia Impact Fund said the investments extend its support for technology entrepreneurs beyond Cambodia.

Carolyne Pung, co-founder of Canadia Impact Fund, said both investments reflect the fund’s view that young people need good information to make education and career decisions, and that digital document verification has room to grow in Cambodia as businesses and public services digitize. The investments can link education and employment in both countries and support secure digital transactions in the region.

Choose & Connect is a free career and study guidance platform for people aged 14 to 25, which brings together information on careers, study options and internships. It was launched in France in 2026 and was founded by Hélène Diep, an engineering graduate of the EPITA school with Cambodian roots.

The investment will support the platform’s development in Cambodia and it aims to help students plan their education and careers and introduce young French graduates to jobs in the country. It is CIFC’s first investment in a French start-up.

Diep said many young people do not have a clear picture of the careers open to them. “We created Choose and Connect to make that information easier to access,” she said.

DOCONCHAIN is a Singapore-headquartered technology company that operates in the Philippines and helps businesses and public institutions sign, notarise, authenticate, and verify digital documents.

It records each action on a private blockchain, helping organizations verify authenticity and detect alterations. It supports San Juan City’s electronic business permit system, which launched in January 2026.

It also partnered with HR technology provider Sprout Solutions to add digital signatures and document verification to Sprout’s systems. Sprout reported in February 2026 that it serves more than 2,000 corporate clients and 180,000 active users.

The investment will support DOCONCHAIN’s growth in Southeast Asia and its exploration of opportunities in Cambodia.

Olivier Bariou, CEO of DOCONCHAIN, said businesses and public institutions can spend a great deal of time managing documents. “We’d like to explore how our technology could be useful in Cambodia and see what we can build together with local partners,” the executive said.

Canadia Impact Fund invests in Cambodian AI startup Newwave

item.title: ADB commits up to $57.5 million to Asia infrastructure fund
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: ADB has committed and will administer up to $57.5 million for a BlackRock-managed infrastructure credit fund focused primarily on Southeast Asia.
item.content:encoded:
The Asian Development Bank has committed and will administer up to $57.5 million for a BlackRock-managed infrastructure credit fund targeting sustainable projects and industrial decarbonization primarily in Southeast Asia.

ADB said it has committed up to $30 million to the Emerging Asia Infrastructure Credit Fund, which is managed by Global Infrastructure Partners, a part of BlackRock. The bank will also administer up to $10 million from the Canadian Climate and Nature Fund for the Private Sector in Asia and up to $17.5 million from the Australian Climate Finance Partnership.

The fund is targeting $750 million and plans to build a portfolio of 10 to 20 investments, according to ADB project documents. It will use senior and mezzanine debt to finance greenfield and brownfield infrastructure and companies working on industrial transition.

Its focus includes the shift to a low-carbon economy, hard-to-abate industries and emerging decarbonization technologies. ADB said the vehicle will operate primarily in Southeast Asia, with eligible markets across developing Asia.

The fund sits under the Industrial Transformation Programme of Financing Asia’s Transition Partnership, or FAST-P, a blended finance initiative launched by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. The structure combines catalytic and commercial capital to reduce investment risks and attract institutional investors.

The Japan International Cooperation Agency is also investing in the fund, while Japan has recognized the project as related to an ADB-Japan energy security initiative. ADB did not disclose JICA’s commitment in the announcement.

TNGlobal previously reported that FAST-P’s Energy Transition Acceleration Finance Partnership raised $250 million at first close. Singapore has pledged up to $500 million in concessional capital across FAST-P, aiming to catalyze as much as $5 billion for Asia’s green transition.

ADB said its participation is intended to expand long-term financing for sustainable infrastructure and demonstrate structures that can attract private capital into developing Asian markets.

Energy Transition Acceleration Finance Partnership under Singapore’s FAST-P initiative raises $250M in first close

item.title: KJTS secures 20-year cooling deal for Bangkok hospital
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: KJTS Group's Thai subsidiary will invest THB22.7 million to upgrade and operate a chiller plant at Synphaet Ramintra Hospital for 20 years.
item.content:encoded:
Malaysia-based KJTS Group has secured a 20-year agreement to upgrade and operate a chiller plant at Synphaet Ramintra Hospital in Bangkok, marking its first cooling-as-a-service project in Thailand’s healthcare sector.

KJTS said its Thai subsidiary, KJTN Engineering Company Limited, signed the design, build and operate agreement with Synphaet Company Limited for the hospital’s Building 2.

KJTN Engineering will fund about THB22.7 million ($700,000) in capital expenditure for the chiller upgrade, construction and project-management work. The subsidiary will design and upgrade the plant, operate and maintain it, and supply chilled water to the hospital.

The agreement provides for a fixed monthly payment and a variable fee based on metered chilled-water consumption, according to KJTS. Ownership of the upgraded chiller plant will transfer to Synphaet when the service period ends.

The retrofit will replace major equipment and add integrated controls and real-time remote monitoring. KJTS said the system will adjust operations according to cooling demand and weather conditions, with the aim of reducing energy consumption while maintaining the hospital’s cooling requirements.

Construction is scheduled to run from December 2026 through May 2027. The 20-year service period is expected to begin in May 2027 and continue through April 2047.

The project extends KJTS’s Thailand business beyond hospitality. The group already manages long-term cooling agreements with several Centara properties, including four 20-year agreements announced in September for hotels in Bangkok, Hua Hin, Pattaya and Koh Samui.

KJTS provides energy-management and facilities-management services in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand. Its cooling-as-a-service model combines upfront investment in equipment with recurring payments for operations, maintenance and chilled-water supply.

Synphaet Ramintra is part of the Synphaet hospital network in Thailand. The parties did not disclose a total contract value, expected revenue contribution or energy-savings target for the hospital project.

item.title: MAS and ABS set PayNow Gen2 rollout through 2028
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: Singapore plans staged PayNow Gen2 upgrades through 2028, covering QR interoperability, deep-linked checkout, government payments and transaction data.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore’s next phase of instant-payment upgrades will move from technical development in 2027 to wider deployment in 2028, with measures covering QR interoperability, mobile checkout links, government payments and richer transaction data.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) released the implementation roadmap for PayNow Generation 2 on Wednesday, following a study with banks, payment providers and government agencies.

The roadmap calls for a limited rollout of SGQR+ in 2027 before broader expansion in 2028. SGQR+ is intended to let merchants accept more domestic and cross-border QR payment schemes through a single commercial arrangement, rather than maintaining separate arrangements for each scheme.

MAS and ABS also plan to establish technical standards and a central facility for PayNow deep-linking by the end of 2027, with wider connections between banks and payment service providers expected in 2028. Deep links can open a customer’s banking app with payment details already populated, reducing the steps required to complete a mobile transaction.

Ant International said its Antom unit has already introduced a deep-linking flow for Lazada Singapore and reported an approximately 9 percent improvement in payment success rates. The company also said its 2C2P unit is working with GovTech Singapore on a proof of concept for GovWallet. Those performance figures and use cases were supplied by Ant International.

The public sector is another focus of the roadmap. A limited rollout for higher-value government payments is planned for late 2027, followed by targeted adoption by other agencies in 2028. PayNow’s current transfer limit is S$200,000, although participating financial institutions may apply lower customer limits.

MAS and ABS said new rules for merchant disputes, refunds and fraud reporting will be introduced in stages from 2028. The program also includes richer structured data fields by the end of 2027, with services using the additional information expected from 2028 onward. These fields could support automated reconciliation, invoice matching and more detailed transaction records for businesses.

The agencies will continue evaluating micropayments and agentic commerce, including safeguards for payments initiated by artificial intelligence systems. MAS said the broader Future Payment Rails Blueprint, covering the architecture of Singapore’s national payment infrastructure, is due in 2027.

MAS, ABS chart instant payments enhancements with PayNow Generation 2 study

item.title: FOMO Pay taps Anchorage Digital for US stablecoin infrastructure
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal
item.description: FOMO Pay will use Anchorage Digital's US stablecoin minting, redemption and trading infrastructure for payment and settlement services.
item.content:encoded:
Singapore-headquartered payment institution FOMO Pay has partnered with Anchorage Digital to connect regulated US stablecoin infrastructure with payment and settlement services across Asia and the Middle East.

FOMO Pay said it became the first Singapore institution onboarded to Anchorage Digital’s US platform. Under the partnership, it will use infrastructure from Anchorage Digital Bank for stablecoin minting and redemption and separately access Anchorage Digital’s trading services.

The companies said the arrangement is intended to support FOMO Pay clients using regulated US dollar stablecoins for payments and commercial settlement. They did not identify a particular stablecoin, disclose transaction volumes or name customers that will use the service.

FOMO Pay said the partnership links Anchorage Digital Bank’s issuance infrastructure with its payment network in Asian and Middle Eastern markets. FOMO Pay is licensed in Singapore, Hong Kong and the Middle East, according to the companies.

Anchorage Digital Bank operates under a US national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. Anchorage Digital also has a Singapore entity licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

The companies plan a later phase that could extend the relationship to digital asset custody for FOMO Pay. That phase is subject to technical, regulatory and compliance requirements and has not been described as live.

Stablecoins are increasingly being evaluated by payment companies for cross-border settlement because they can transfer value outside conventional banking hours. Regulators in Singapore and other Asian markets are also developing frameworks intended to distinguish regulated payment tokens and service providers from unlicensed activity.

The partnership is FOMO Pay’s latest move involving digital-asset payment infrastructure. The company provides collection, payout, treasury and payment services to businesses and financial institutions, while Anchorage Digital supplies custody, trading, settlement and issuance infrastructure to institutional clients.

Neither company disclosed the commercial terms of the agreement or a timetable for broader client availability. FOMO Pay said the initial work centers on minting, redemption and trading access, with custody to be considered separately.

US’s Anchorage Digital expands in Asia with five new institutional partners

item.title: Singapore-based Liquid Group, Japan’s NETSTARS launch cross-border QR payments in Japan via RoamQRTM, JPQR Global
item.dc:creator: Duc Dao
item.description: Travelers from Singapore can now pay by QR code at various merchants in Japan using familiar Singapore payment apps, following the launch of a cross-border corridor between Liquid Group's RoamQR network and Japan's JPQR Global payment system.
item.content:encoded:
Travelers from Singapore can now pay by QR code at various merchants in Japan using familiar Singapore payment apps, following the launch of a cross-border corridor between Liquid Group‘s RoamQR network and Japan’s JPQR Global payment system.

In a statement on Wednesday, Netstars, the operator of JPQR Global, said the corridor was announced at the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026. It links Liquid Group, a Singapore-headquartered payments infrastructure company, with NETSTARS, a Tokyo-based payment gateway company.

Users of participating Singapore payment apps can scan QR codes that display the JPQR Global acceptance mark, without downloading a separate app. JPQR Global has been adding merchants across Japan, particularly in popular tourist areas, and plans to add more.

JPQR Global is a framework for cross-border QR payments between Japan’s unified QR standard, JPQR, and the QR standards of partner countries. Launched in July 2025 at Expo 2025 Osaka, it already connects with Cambodia’s KHQR and Indonesia’s QRIS for inbound payments in Japan. The Singapore connection is its third partner country.

Yoshio Fukuda, general director and board member of the Payments Japan Association, said expanding the number of connected countries makes stays in Japan more convenient for international visitors and helps Japanese merchants win more inbound spending. The association plans to expand usage and merchant acceptance and to enable outbound payments from Japan.

Tsuyoshi Ri, president and CEO of NETSTARS, said connecting RoamQR with JPQR Global, after the Cambodia and Indonesia links, is an important step for the company’s borderless payments goal.

Jeremy Tan, CEO of Liquid Group, said the company’s RoamQR network connects domestic payment systems so they can work across borders without each provider building separate integrations.

Samsung, ShopeePay expand payments tie-up, enabling QR payments in Singapore and Vietnam

item.title: SEA’s digital consumer credit loan book reaches estimated $19.8 billion at the end of first half
item.dc:creator: TNGlobal Staff
item.description: Southeast Asia’s digital consumer credit loan book reached an estimated $19.8 billion at the end of the first half of 2026, according to Momentum Works’ latest report.
item.content:encoded:
Southeast Asia’s digital consumer credit loan book reached an estimated $19.8 billion at the end of the first half of 2026, according to Momentum Works’ latest report.

The Consumer Credit in Southeast Asia 2026 report showed on Monday that Indonesia leads the region with $8.6 billion in outstanding loans, followed by the Philippines at $4.3 billion and Thailand at US$2.9 billion.

Sea Group’s Monee alone makes up about 45 percent of the total loan book, making it the largest lender in the region.

Monee’s reported loan book reached $12.6 billion in the third quarter of 2026 (including Brazil and SME lending), nearly quadrupling since the first quarter of 2024.

Personal cash loans and off-Shopee Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) now account for about 60 percent of Monee’s total loan book, while its standalone apps are among the top of the Finance category app rankings in their respective markets.

The top four players, Monee, Grab, GoTo and GCash, account for about 60 percent.

Meanwhile, the report highlighted that TikTok Shop will almost certainly scale its own consumer credit business in Southeast Asia.

It noted that TikTok Shop brings a sizeable commerce operation, transaction data and access to ByteDance’s experience developing consumer credit through Douyin in China.

Its lending arm PIPO (Payments In, Payments Out) is already offering financing in Thailand, the Philippines and Malaysia, using different local arrangements.

Momentum Works believes its new standalone shopping app gives TikTok Shop greater freedom to integrate and promote credit, supporting both purchase conversion and lending growth.

Grab’s proposed acquisition of Atome Financial, on the other hand, shows the value of combining lending expertise with platform distribution.

As platforms bring credit in-house, Momentum Works said independent BNPL providers face growing pressure. Market consolidation puts greater pressure on independent BNPL providers than on established cash lenders.

The report also showed that large platforms and wallets are best placed to capture the next wave of credit growth.

Momentum Works sees substantial room for growth in the region’s US$19.8 billion digital consumer credit market, with large players likely to capture much of the upside, provided execution remains disciplined and regulation stable.

The window for new independent players to achieve scale and venture-level exits has closed, it added.

Southeast Asia content commerce to reach $77.9B in 2026 as live goes mainstream – Momentum Works
